Interview Experience​
Kevin Shah - TY BTech CE, 231070060 
 
 
 
Introduction 
I am Kevin Shah, currently in my third year of pursuing a BTech Degree in Computer 
Engineering at Veermata Jijabai Technological Institute, Matunga. 
 
This report will serve as a record of my experience interviewing with HSBC. 
 
 
 
1

Pre-Placement Talk 
On 13 August 2025, we received an email from TPO informing us that HSBC will be visiting 
the campus for intern hiring. In this email, there was a link for applying on the official HSBC 
Careers page. 
A week later we got an email from HSBC regarding the upcoming schedule of online 
PPT(Pre-Placement Talk) and the OA(Online Assessment). 
Platform: Zoom Webinar 
Date & Time: 22 August 2025, 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM 
The Pre-Placement Talk is one of the most important parts of any internship drive and it’s 
imperative that you pay heed to the PPT. It is also advisable that you take notes of some 
key points that are being discussed by the panelists as there are high chances of those 
topics being discussed in the interviews. So I’d suggest either taking screenshots during the 
session or making notes of important points which you may go through before the 
interview. 
All the company related information will be conveyed in the PPT like its history, business 
model, etc which you can further refer to on their website also once because it is really 
important to study about the company well in advance. 
P.S: One of my friends recorded the entire session and was kind enough to share it with 
me, which I watched again before the interview so that I do not miss even the minute 
details. 
 
Online Assessment 
Participants: Everyone who had received the PPT link 
The OA consisted of two rounds i.e. the SImulate Test and the Codility Test. 
 
2

And both these rounds were conducted immediately after the PPT. 
Round 1: Simulate Test(167 students appeared for this) 
Time: 4.30 pm to 5.40 pm 
This round consisted of general HR based questions and Situational judgement, personality 
+ formal/informal questions on their internal platform. 
Even though it was supposed to be a 70 minute test, people went on for 2 hours because 
there was no time limit set on their platform. Due to this those who did not submit the test 
on time were disqualified.  
The test was easy but very lengthy because there were several sections and a lot of 
questions within each of them.  
I had watched this video a few days before the test and got a similar set of questions: 
 
How I would prepare for the HSBC Simulate Assessment
 
Round 2: Codility Test(110 students appeared for this) 
Time: 7 pm 
After the Simulate Test, the shortlisted students received the link for the Codility Test. Again 
it was conducted on their internal platform only and the duration of the test was 100 
minutes.  
It consisted of 3 easy to medium DSA questions covering arrays, math and logic based 
questions. ​
​
Question 1: Given a string containing only digits ‘6’ and ‘9’, replace at most one digit 
(6->9,9->6) to make the largest integer possible. 
For example: 
Input: num=”996996” Output:”999996” 
 
3

Interview Day 
Date: 2 September 2025 
We were asked to report at 8.30 am, and the interviews were scheduled to begin at 9.30 
am. Additionally we were also asked to bring our own laptops and headsets because the 
interviews were going to be completely virtual but from college itself.  
I wore a dark green full sleeves shirt, along with black trousers because for financial firms 
and MNCs, your attire matters a lot, so dress well. 
Some general tips: 
●​ Keep a 2 to 3 minute long intro ready because this is what is going to drive your 
entire interview. 
●​ The entire process can be very tiring and time taking so it is important to stay 
hydrated throughout so drink plenty of water. 
●​ If you know your interview is a bit later, then ask your friends to tell you about what 
questions they were asked because there is a high chance that those questions 
might get repeated for you. 
●​ Stay confident while answering and DO NOT LIE because the interviewer will catch it 
within no time so please do not fake it. 
Technical Round: 
There were 2 panels for the technical round and I was allocated the 1st panel. But before 
me around 4-5 students had their interviews so I asked everyone about what questions 
they were asked. This gives you an edge only if your interview is scheduled in the middle or 
later.  
Finally I was called for my interview and I took a deep breath before entering the room to 
calm myself, as this was my first interview during the entire Internship drive, I was a bit 
nervous in the beginning. 
 
9

The interviewer briefly introduced himself first and then asked me to introduce myself. I 
had prepared my introduction well in advance and had practised it in my mock interviews 
as well so I covered my branch along with CGPA, my projects, competitions and hackathons 
that I had participated in and lastly hobbies. I’d like to stretch upon this because this is 
what is going to decide the entire flow of your interview. Since I had mentioned that “I like 
to watch Sci-Fi movies in my free time”, the interviewer replied to that by saying “Even I am 
a big fan of Sci-Fi, have you watched {xyz}”. So this builds a good connection if the common 
interests align.. 
After which the interviewer directly jumped to the questions and asked me to explain my 
favorite project. To which I started explaining the one I did in Project X, where I covered the 
entire flow by following the STAR method which my seniors had suggested. Since it was an 
ML-based project, it is important to highlight the numbers i.e. the size of the dataset used, 
the accuracies which you got, etc. It’s important that you keep all these stats in mind 
because there were cross questions and an in-depth discussion based on the approach I 
had used and how I improvised further. I also explained my mini project very briefly that I 
had made during that time frame in order to understand a few underlying concepts. The 
interviewer seemed satisfied and moved to the next section which was the CS 
Fundamentals. 
He asked me about the 4 pillars of OOPs, to which I answered all the 4 one by one with 
examples and use cases. It is important to give examples because it would give an 
impression that you really understand the concepts well, so I tried to give 1-2 examples in 
each. Also a few other concepts he wanted to test, so he asked me about method 
overloading, overriding, etc. Then he moved to a few basic questions in DBMS. I don’t 
exactly remember what was asked to me but they were quite straightforward. I was not 
asked anything related to OS or CN but if you have time then I would highly recommend 
you to study these subjects as well. 
After wrapping up CS Fundamentals, he moved on to DSA. He asked me a fairly easy 
recursion question which he told me to code on an online compiler. I was explaining the 
logic as I typed because it is important to think out loud, so I quickly gave the reasoning 
behind every line of code. After writing it fully, I gave a dry run on 2 examples and finally 
concluded by stating the time and space complexity.  
 
10

The DSA part concluded here and the interviewer asked me if I have any questions for him. 
I then asked 2 questions from what I had read in the latest articles and it’s important to ask 
questions because it shows your curiosity to learn more about the firm. I don’t exactly 
remember what I had asked but one of them was related to quantum computing which the 
firm had integrated. I thanked the interviewer at the end with a smile on my face and went 
back to have my lunch. 
HR Round: 
After the lunch break following the technical round, 6 students were sent for the HR round 
which consisted of only 1 panel.  
Again I was 4th or 5th so I asked other people what questions they had. 
This round included some basic HR based questions and was concluded in approximately 
10 minutes. These were asked to me: 
1.​ Basic intro 
2.​ Family background 
3.​ Do you want to pursue masters? 
4.​ Why HSBC(Try and recollect points from PPT) 
5.​ Some scenario based questions(You’ll find these in GFG articles) 
6.​ Tech Stack you use 
This was a chill round but it’s important to stay confident and answer all the questions 
honestly. 
After our interviews we waited for the results and were roaming in the college, but then the 
TPO CRs requested all of us to go home as they were still processing the results. 
Results: 
The results came out at around 10 PM, and fortunately, I was among the selected 
candidates. Three of my friends also received offers.
